title: From Optimal to Practical: Efficient Micro-op Cache Replacement Policies for Data Center Applications
problem: Data center applications suffer frequent micro-op (uop) cache misses because no effective uop-cache-specific replacement policy exists; the uop cache has fundamentally different cost characteristics from conventional caches (variable and disproportional miss costs, partial hits), making standard policies like LRU and even Belady's algorithm suboptimal.
motivation: The CPU frontend is a major energy and performance bottleneck for data center applications, and improving uop cache utilization is critical—but without a theoretical near-optimal bound for uop caches, it is impossible to know how much improvement is achievable or how to design toward it.
method: FLACK is an offline algorithm (one with knowledge of all future instruction accesses) that computes optimal micro-op cache evictions by accounting for how these caches differ from regular ones: re-fetching evicted instructions is much more expensive, and instruction groups may be partially cached. This beats standard algorithms like Belady's because it optimizes for these unique costs. FURBYS then implements this strategy for real-world online use (without future knowledge) through three techniques: (1) measuring which instructions hit or miss across a full program run, (2) detecting locally or temporarily hot instruction patterns, and (3) ignoring entries with low hit rates when choosing what to evict.
key_novelty: FLACK is a near-optimal offline replacement algorithm for micro-op caches that accounts for their unique costs—expensive instruction re-fetches and partial instruction caching—and provides a new theoretical bound for practical policy design.
contributions: FLACK near-optimal offline policy for uop caches, showing 4.46% greater miss reduction than Belady's algorithm
Establishment of a new theoretical upper bound for uop cache replacement policy improvement
FURBYS practical profile-guided policy achieving 14.34% average miss reduction vs. LRU (1.84x over state-of-the-art)
3.10% performance-per-watt improvement; FURBYS equivalent to LRU on 1.5x uop cache size (up to 2x)

metrics.other: 14.34% average miss reduction over LRU (1.84x over state-of-the-art); FLACK: 30.21% average miss reduction bound, 4.46% greater than Belady

baselines: Belady's algorithm (offline optimal for conventional caches)
current state-of-the-art uop cache replacement policy
limitations: FURBYS relies on offline profiling and may not adapt well to workloads with significant phase changes between profiling and production runs.
primary_theme: Near-optimal uop cache replacement policy design from theoretical bound to practical profile-guided implementation
